verdicts.evidence: KICKOFF.md lines 202-203: 'Use the\ndiagram skill for the architecture diagrams' (verified verbatim at those line numbers). SKILL.md line 18: 'Write mermaid for the user's request. Rules:' (verified verbatim).
verdicts.reasoning: The diagram skill is subject-agnostic — Step 1 literally says to write mermaid 'for the user's request', deriving the slug from 'the diagram's subject' (line 24). It has no built-in notion of what to diagram; that is supplied entirely by the caller. Naming the subject as 'the architecture diagrams' is the invocation argument, not a restatement of any methodology the skill already owns. Correctly classified load-bearing-parameter; low severity because it's a single noun-phrase, not a structural addition.

verdicts.evidence: KICKOFF.md lines 203-205: 'its artifact contract is the editable `.mmd` source plus rendered `.svg`/`.png` (optionally `.excalidraw`), committed as a pair, so don't hand-draw or paste a flattened image in its place' (verified verbatim). SKILL.md line 8: 'Every run emits an **artifact set**, never a dead pixel dump:' followed immediately by the artifact table at lines 10-14: `<slug>.mmd` (mermaid source), `<slug>.svg` + `<slug>.png` (rendered), `<slug>.excalidraw` (optional, flowcharts only) — verified verbatim.
verdicts.reasoning: The KICKOFF sentence re-enumerates exactly the three-row artifact table the skill already fixes for every invocation (mmd source / svg+png rendered / optional excalidraw) and re-teaches the skill's own 'never a dead pixel dump' motto (line 8) plus its hard rule at line 55 ('A `.mmd` file alone is not a diagram... never ship without rendering') as 'don't hand-draw or paste a flattened image in its place'. This is the skill's own fixed output contract being spelled out again for the caller rather than an invocation-specific parameter. One nuance keeps this from being pure restatement: 'committed as a pair' is a git-workflow convention the skill never states (the skill only notes the outdir 'can' be a git repo the user may commit into, line 24) — but that phrase is incidental framing on top of an otherwise fully-duplicated artifact list, not enough to flip the claim. Medium severity: it's a full sentence of duplicated methodology, not a single word, but low practical friction since it doesn't misstate anything.

verdicts.evidence: KICKOFF.md lines 205-209: 'Keep that pair current as the design moves, and keep the Mermaid embedded in the SDD in sync with it: step 14's drift check never opens `.mmd` or `.svg` at all — it extracts entity names from the ASCII and Mermaid blocks inside the markdown docs and cross-references them against the diff, and it only reports advisory findings. Nothing downstream catches a stale source file for you.' (verified verbatim). Full 61-line SKILL.md read end-to-end; grep -niE 'sync|stale|current|embed|drift|commit' over the whole file returns only line 24 (git-repo outdir note) and line 56 ('For diagrams destined for a markdown doc or PDF pipeline that renders ```mermaid``` fences natively, embed the mermaid source rather than the PNG — it stays diffable and editable.'). The only re-render trigger the skill defines is line 50's 'Iteration loop: when the user wants changes to the diagram's content or structure, edit the `.mmd` source and re-run Step 2' — a user-request-triggered regeneration of SVG/PNG from `.mmd`, not an ongoing duty to keep a doc-embedded Mermaid copy synced with the `.mmd` as the design evolves elsewhere.
verdicts.reasoning: I independently hunted the full skill file (no references/ subdirectory exists to also check) for any concept of syncing an embedded copy against its source over time, using the required synonym sweep (sync, stale, current, embed, drift, commit) rather than trusting the queue's quotes. Nothing surfaces. The skill does anticipate embedding (line 56) as one of two delivery modes, but never addresses what happens when the `.mmd` is later edited while a copy already lives inside another markdown doc (e.g. SDD.md) — its iteration loop only covers explicit user-requested edits to the standalone artifact set, not proactive drift-prevention for an embedded duplicate. The KICKOFF text is therefore load-bearing: it's telling the operator to manually own a maintenance duty the skill has no mechanism for, and explaining why (downstream step 14 only advisory-checks entity names in docs, never reopens `.mmd`/`.svg`). Confirmed as a genuine unenforced-gap; medium severity because a stale embedded diagram silently diverging from the real architecture is a real correctness risk, but it's caught eventually by human review rather than causing a hard failure.
